perspective:
Vincent’s accessible information:

- He is a mechanic and long-time friend of Patrick, a construction worker. They met as teenagers, share blue-collar work, and sometimes collaborate.
- At the diner, Vincent knows Patrick is considering a new construction venture. Patrick tells him it seems like a good opportunity to expand his business. Vincent has heard it is risky. Patrick says he thinks it is worth the risk but is still weighing options. Vincent warns about financial insecurity and suggests reconsidering or delaying until more information is gathered. Patrick thanks him and says he will think it over.
- A few days later, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent tells Patrick he feels Patrick is not telling him everything. Patrick says it is complicated and he did not want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent says he feels betrayed and that as a friend he needs transparency. Patrick apologizes, admits he should have been more open, and offers to explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, after their detailed discussion, Vincent learns the situation is serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick gratefully accepts.
- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent says it looks like the venture might actually turn a profit. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees and says they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick discuss drafting a business plan for their joint venture. Vincent says their combined skills can make it a success and that they need to outline every step carefully. Patrick agrees and says they should cover all bases. Vincent participates in the planning.
